paper.title: Language Generation with Replay: A Learning-Theoretic View of Model Collapse
paper.summary: Introduces endogenous replay of a generator's earlier outputs, proves that replay preserves uniform generation but separates non-uniform and unrestricted limit generation, gives Witness Protection for countable classes, and establishes proper-generation lower bounds.

formalization_scope.summary: Theorems 4.1, 5.1, 6.1, 6.6, and 7.3 are fully formalized at their stated deterministic interfaces. Theorem 6.1 combines the arbitrary-countable-domain semantic theorem with an executable literal persistent-cutoff machine and an explicit finite-query realization on the normalized natural-number universe. Theorem 7.1 has its exact adaptive-machine statement and checked diagonal reduction, while the recursive Algorithm 3 construction remains open.
specializations: Countable classes are explicit Nat-indexed families, preserving order and allowing repeated extensionally equal languages.
Theorem 4.1 exposes the source's positive sample-threshold convention explicitly.
Theorem 5.1 uses the support-isomorphic two-copy domain Sum Nat Nat in place of positive and negative integers.
Theorem 6.6 uses Sum Int Nat, with zero-based marker n representing the source marker star-to-the-n-plus-one.
Theorem 6.1 transports the semantic natural-number construction to an arbitrary countable domain by a classically chosen equivalence.
Theorem 6.1's executable finite-query realization is stated on the source's normalized natural-number universe.
gaps: Theorem 7.1 still assumes the Algorithm 3 recursive-family certificate construction.
Lemma 7.2's printed termination split omits a machine that asks finitely many queries and then silently diverges; a total small-step model or a clock/dovetailing repair is needed.
No uniform query-complexity, running-time, extracted implementation, separate Mathlib Computable specialization, or independent human correspondence audit is claimed.

audit_refs.scope: AI-assisted comparison of the six headline theorems and their supporting definitions and lemmas against the SHA-256-pinned arXiv v2 PDF; no human certification is claimed.
Generated declaration-existence, defining-module, and axiom-allowlist checks for the P22 claim-linked endpoints.

exclusions: Definitions 3.1--3.5, Definition 6.2, Algorithms 1--3, and Lemmas 6.3--6.5, 6.7--6.8, and 7.2 are mapped in the PaperMap or through their headline theorem rather than assigned independent cards.
Background results recalled from earlier papers are reused through existing library declarations rather than duplicated as P22 claims.
claim_inventory.notes: Complete means every theorem in the paper's six-item headline inventory has a card. Theorem 6.1's semantic and finite-query components are complete; the construction premise of Theorem 7.1 remains open.

lean_declaration_inventory.scope_description: The seven source-facing Results endpoints (with separate semantic and finite-query endpoints for Theorem 6.1), the exact Theorem 7.1 proposition, and the diagnostic for the obsolete over-strong Algorithm 3 obligation.
exclusions: Paper-local replay definitions, state-machine invariants, adversarial-stream helpers, and supporting lemmas are documented in the PaperMap but are not separate claim-linked endpoints.
The restart-normalized Witness Protection machine remains a proved implementation variant behind the source-facing carried-cutoff facade.
lean_declaration_inventory.notes: Complete is relative to the selected claim-linked declarations, not every declaration below the P22 umbrella.

claims.title: Uniform generation is unchanged by replay
claims.statement_summary: A UUS hypothesis class is uniformly generatable with replay exactly when it is uniformly generatable ordinarily, without increasing the sample threshold.

formalization.notes: Lean proves the fixed-threshold equivalence and preserves the same positive threshold. The proof itself does not need the source's standing UUS assumption.

lean_links.notes: The source's one-based positive threshold is explicit in the Lean signature.

claims.title: Replay separates non-uniform generation
claims.statement_summary: A countable UUS class is non-uniformly generatable ordinarily but not non-uniformly generatable with replay.

formalization.notes: Lean constructs the source adversary recursively and reuses the existing countable-class theorem for the ordinary positive half.

lean_links.notes: Sum Nat Nat replaces the source's positive and negative integer copies without changing the support incidence structure.

claims.title: Witness Protection generates every countable class under replay
claims.statement_summary: A universal membership-query-only generator generates in the limit with replay every countable UUS hypothesis class over a countable domain.

formalization.notes: The semantic replay-generation theorem is complete on arbitrary countable domains. On the normalized natural-number universe, the literal carried-cutoff machine is executable relative to the Boolean oracle and every round exposes a finite valid answered-query cache with an explicit cutoff-dependent cardinality bound. An extensional locality theorem proves that any oracle agreeing on the cache produces the same transition. A separate Mathlib Computable specialization is an optional strengthening, not a source-theorem gap.

components.summary: The persistent-cutoff Witness Protection generator is eventually fresh and target-valid on every replay enumeration over any countable domain.

Every literal carried-cutoff round is executable relative to the Boolean oracle and has an explicit finite answered-query cache that covers all tests through termination and extensionally determines the transition.

lean_links.notes: The wrapper selects the literal carried-cutoff construction and transports it from Nat to the source's arbitrary countable domain.

The trace is an exhaustive finite answer cache. At an active round it covers all family indices below the round and every sure-set or finite-prefix point through the first admissible cutoff; at an inactive round it covers all consistency tests. Any second valid family oracle returning the same cached answers yields exactly the same transition.

claims.title: Replay separates generation in the limit on a general class
claims.statement_summary: There is an uncountable UUS hypothesis class that is generatable in the ordinary limit model but not generatable in the limit with replay.

formalization.notes: Lean formalizes the literal marker-padded two-subclass witness and proves both Lemma 6.7 and Lemma 6.8, together with UUS and uncountability.

lean_links.notes: The source headline states the separation; Lean additionally exposes the witness class's uncountability and UUS properties.

claims.title: Membership queries alone are insufficient for universal proper generation
claims.statement_summary: No deterministic membership-query-only generator properly generates in the limit every countable recursive UUS hypothesis class.

source_assessment.notes: The printed Lemma 7.2 considers rounds that terminate after finitely many queries and rounds that issue infinitely many queries, but omits finite-query silent divergence. The headline theorem may still be repairable with a total small-step model or clock/dovetailing argument.

formalization.notes: Lean pins the exact impossibility proposition, models deterministic adaptive membership-query rounds, and verifies that any Algorithm 3 certificate contradicts universality. Constructing the recursive family certificate remains open.

components.summary: The exact universal impossibility proposition is represented over deterministic adaptive membership-query machines and uniformly recursive UUS families.
Any valid Algorithm 3 recursive-family certificate refutes the tested machine's universal proper-generation guarantee.
Under the universal-generator contradiction hypothesis, Algorithm 3 constructs a total recursive UUS family and completed adversarial execution certificate.

lean_links.notes: The statement makes per-round termination and eventual proper containment explicit.
The recursive Algorithm 3 construction is an explicit premise and is not hidden by the facade.
A query-forever machine refutes the obsolete obligation quantified over every computable machine; the source-facing obligation is restricted to a machine assumed universal.

claims.title: Four languages separate proper replay generation
claims.statement_summary: There exists a finite UUS hypothesis class that is not properly generatable in the limit with replay.

formalization.notes: Lean uses the source's four integer languages and checks all four cases of the first proper output.

lean_links.notes: The source headline asks for some finite class; Lean exposes its exact four-member UUS witness.
